title: Definition
body_md:
Let $X$ be a geometrically integral variety $X$ over $K$. We say that $X$ satiesfies \textbf{strong approximation off $S$} (SA) if
\[
\overline{X(K)}=pr^{S}(X(\mathbb{A}_{K})).
\]
head: environment

title: Conjecture
body_md:
Assume $X$ satisfies strong approximation off a finite set of primes $S$ of $K$. Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$ with
$\mathrm{codim}(X-U,X)\geq2$. Does $U$ also satisfies strong approximation off $S$?
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
We say that $X$ satisfies \textbf{strong approximation with Brauer-Manin obstruction} off $S$ if
\[
\overline{X(K)}=pr^{S}(X(\mathbb{A}_{K})^{\mathrm{Br}(X)}).
\]
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
A smooth $K$-variety $X$ satisfies \textbf{arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction} ($\mathrm{APSABM}$) off $S$ if, for every open subvariety $U\subseteq X$ satisfying
\[
  \operatorname{codim}_X(X\setminus U)\geq 2,
\]
we have
\[
\overline{U(K)}=pr^{S}(U(\mathbb{A}_{K})^{\mathrm{Br}(U)}).
\]
head: environment

title: Definition
head: environment

label: main thm
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main thm}
Assume that $X$ admits a positive linear torsor presentation. Then $X$ satisfies $(\mathrm{APSABM})$ off $\varnothing$. Moreover, if the structure group $G$ is of multiplicative type, then $X$ satisfies $(\mathrm{APSABM}_{1})$ off $\varnothing$.
head: environment

label: Purity of toric
title: Corollary
body_md: \label{Purity of toric} Let $X$ be a smooth toric variety with $K[X]=K$, then $X$ admits a positive linear torsor presentation. Hence $X$ satiesfies $(\mathrm{APSABM}_{1})$ off $\varnothing$.
head: environment

label: P^1-connected
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $X$ be a smooth toric variety over a field of characteristic zero with $K[X]=K$. Let $\hat{G}=\mathrm{Pic}(\overline{X})$. Then we have a natural isomorphism of sets:
\[
X(K)/\sim_{\mathbb{P}^1,\mathrm{ch}}\cong H^1(K,G).
\]
head: environment

label: prp:scaled-approximation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prp:scaled-approximation}
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, let
\[
  \lambda:\mathbb G_m\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)
\]
be a $K$-cocharacter whose weights are strictly positive, and let $Y=V\setminus Z$ be a $\lambda$-stable open subset with $\operatorname{codim}_{V}Z\geq2$.

Given non-empty open subsets
\[
W_{f}\subset Y(\mathbb{A}^{f}_{K}),\quad  W_{\infty}\subset Y(K_{\infty}).
\]
There exists $y\in Y(K)$ and $r\in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ such that
\[
y_{f}\in W_{f},\quad y_{\infty}\in \lambda(r)W_{\infty}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First assume $K=\mathbb{Q}$. Let $n=\mathrm{dim}(V)$ and 
\[
\lambda(c)(y_{1},...,y_{n})=(c^{a_{1}}y_{1},...,c^{a_{n}}y_{n})
\]
 

Changing the signs of the weight-basis vectors if necessary, we may assume $W_\infty\cap\mathbb R_{>0}^n\neq \varnothing$ and fix an element $w\in W_\infty\cap\mathbb R_{>0}^n$.
By (\cite{MR3873133}, proposition 4.6), we have
\[
Y(\mathbb{Q})\cap(Y^{+}(\mathbb{R})\times W_{f})\neq \varnothing
\]
Hence there exists $b\in Y(\mathbb{Q})$ such that $b_{f}\in W_{f}$ and $b_{\infty}>0$. Now consider the following morphism:
\[
\Phi_{b}:\mathbb{A}^{n}_{\mathbb{Q}}\to V\cong\mathbb{A}^{n}_{\mathbb{Q}},\quad (t_{i})\mapsto (b_{i}t^{a_{i}}_{i}).
\]
Note that $\Phi_{b}(ct)=\lambda(c)\Phi_{b}(t)$.

Let $Y_{b}:=\Phi_{b}^{-1}(Y)$, since $\Phi_{b}$ is faithfully flat, the preimage $Y_{b}$ is again an open subset of affine space with co-dimensional two complement. Moreover, $\Phi_{b}^{-1}(W_{f})$ is non-empty since it contains $1$, and $\Phi_{b}^{-1}(W_{\infty})$ is non-empty since $(\frac{w_{i}}{b_{i}})^{1/a_{i}}$ maps to $w\in W_{\infty}$.

Let $B\subset \Phi^{-1}_{b,\infty}(W_{\infty})\cap \mathbb{R}^{n}_{+}$ be a convex open ball and let $v_{1},...,v_{n}\in B\cap \mathbb{Q}^{n}$ be linearly independent vectors. Then we define an automorphism of affine space:
\[
\theta:\mathbb{A}^{n}\to \mathbb{A}^{n},\quad z\mapsto \sum^{n}_{j=1}z_{j}v_{j}
\]
For $z\in \mathbb{R}^n_{+}$, define $r(z):=\sum^{n}_{j=1}z_{j}$. Then the convexity of $B$ gives 
\[
\frac{\theta(z)}{r(z)}\in B.
\]
Now let $U_{f}=(\Phi_{b}\circ \theta)^{-1}(W_{f})$. Applying (\cite{MR3873133}, proposition 4.6) to $U_{f}$ yields an element $z_{0}\in \theta^{-1}(Y_{b})(\mathbb{Q}),$ such that
\[
z_{0}\in \mathbb{R}^{n}_{+},\quad (\Phi_{b}\circ \theta)(z_{0})\in W_{f}.
\]
Finally, let $y=\Phi_{b}(\theta(z_{0}))\in Y(\mathbb{Q})$ and $r=r(z_{0})$. Then
\[
y_{\infty}=\lambda(r)\Phi_{b}(\frac{\theta(z_{0})}{r})\in \lambda(r)\Phi_{b}(B)\subset \lambda(r)W_{\infty}.
\]
In the general case, let $d=[K:\mathbb{Q}]$ and take
\[
  \widetilde Y=\operatorname{Res}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}Y\subseteq
  \widetilde V=\operatorname{Res}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}V\simeq\mathbb A_\mathbb{Q}^{dn}.
\]
Let $Z=V\setminus Y$. Then base change to $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ gives
\[
  (\widetilde V\setminus\widetilde Y)_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}
  =\bigcup_{\sigma:K\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}
    \left(Z^\sigma\times\prod_{\tau\ne\sigma}V^\tau\right).
\]
Each term has dimension at most $(n-2)+(d-1)n=dn-2$. There are natural identifications
\[
  \begin{aligned}
    \widetilde Y(\mathbb{Q})=Y(K),\quad
    \widetilde Y(\mathbb{R})=Y(K_\infty),\quad
    \widetilde Y(\mathbb A_\mathbb{Q}^f)&=Y(\mathbb A_K^f).
  \end{aligned}
\]
Restricting the $\lambda$-action to the
diagonal $\mathbb G_m\subseteq\operatorname{Res}_{K/\mathbb{Q}}\mathbb G_m$ repeats every original
weight $d$ times. Hence the general case follows from the $K=\mathbb{Q}$ case.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md: Let $\xi\in H^1(K,G)$ and consider the twist $V^{\xi}$. Then $V^{\xi}$ is (non-canonically) isomorphic to the affine space, and $\lambda$ descends to $V^{\xi}$ as a cocharacter with positive weights.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As the action $\rho:G\to \mathrm{GL}(V)$ is linear, the twist $V^{\xi}$ is a vector bundle over $\mathrm{Spec}(K)$ and is isomorphic to the affine space.

Now we define a cocharacter $\lambda^{\xi}:\mathbb{G}_{m}\to \mathrm{GL}(V^{\xi})$ as:
\[
\lambda^{\xi}(t)[p,v]:=[p,\rho(\lambda(t))v].
\]
It is well-defined since $\lambda(t)\in Z(G)$.

Let $V=\bigoplus_a V_a$ for the weight decomposition under
$\rho\circ\lambda$. Each $V_a$ is
$G$-stable Since $\lambda$ is central. Hence
\[
V^\xi=\bigoplus_a (P\times^G V_a).
\]
The induced action of $\mathbb G_m$ on $P\times^G V_a$ is multiplication by $t^a$, and
$\dim_K(P\times^G V_a)=\dim_K V_a$. Thus $\lambda^\xi$ has the same weights as
$\rho\circ\lambda$ with the same multiplicities. In particular,
all weights of $\lambda^{\xi}$ are positive.
head: environment

label: codim 2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{codim 2}
The open immersion $Y_U\subseteq V$ satisfies
\[
  \operatorname{codim}_V(V\setminus Y_U)\geq2.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $q$ is a torsor under the smooth group $G$, it is smooth and faithfully flat.  Therefore
\[
  \operatorname{codim}_Y q^{-1}(X\setminus U)
  =
  \operatorname{codim}_X(X\setminus U)
  \geq2.
\]
Let $Z$ be the closure of $q^{-1}(X\setminus U)$ in $V$.  If $Z$ contains a codimension-one irreducible component $E$, then $E$ could not be contained in $V\setminus Y$.  Hence $E\cap Y$ would be a codimension-one subset of $Y$ contained in $q^{-1}(X\setminus U)$, a contradiction, and the result follows.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $x\in U(\mathbb A_K)^{\operatorname{Br}(U)}$. When $G$ is of multiplicative type, we choose $x\in U(\mathbb{A}_{K})^{\mathrm{Br}_{1}(U)}$. Let
$\mathcal N$ be an open neighbourhood of $x$ in
$U(\mathbb A_K)$.

By (\cite{CDX19}, Theorem 3.5) , there exist $\xi\in H^1(K,G)$ and 
  $\eta\in Y_U^\xi(\mathbb A_K)$,
such that $p_U^\xi(\eta)=x$. Let $f=p^{\xi}_{U}$.

The central cocharacter descends to $V^\xi$ with the same
positive weights. We continue to denote it by $\lambda$;
it preserves $Y^{\xi}_{U}$ and satisfies
\[
  f(\lambda(t)y)=f(y).
\]
There exists nonempty open subsets
\[
  W_f\subseteq Y^{\xi}_{U}(\mathbb A_K^f),
  \qquad
  W_\infty\subseteq Y^{\xi}_{U}(K_\infty)
\]
such that
\[
  \eta\in W_f\times W_\infty
  \subseteq f^{-1}(\mathcal N).
\]
By Proposition \ref{prp:scaled-approximation}, there exist
$y\in Y^{\xi}_{U}(K)$ and $r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$ satisfying
\[
  y_f\in W_f,\qquad
  y_\infty\in\lambda(r)W_\infty.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \eta':=(y_f,\lambda(r)^{-1}y_\infty)
  \in W_f\times W_\infty.
\]
Since $f$ is invariant under $\lambda$, the element
$u:=f(y)=f(\eta')\in\mathcal N$. And we conclude the theorem as $x$ and $\mathcal N$ were arbitrary.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{cox torsor}
There is a natural $G$-torsor
\[
  p:Y\longrightarrow X.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  \operatorname{codim}_V(V\setminus Y)\geq 2.
  \tag{5.5}\label{eq:cox-codim}
\]

label: positive weight
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{positive weight}
There are positive integers $a_\rho>0$, constant on Galois orbits in $\Sigma(1)$, such that
\[
  \sum_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}a_\rho v_\rho=0.
  \tag{5.7}\label{positive-relation}
\]
Moreover, there is a $K$-cocharacter
\[
  \lambda:\mathbb G_m\longrightarrow G
\]
whose action on $V_{\overline K}$ is
\[
  \lambda(t)\cdot z_\rho=t^{a_\rho}z_\rho.
\]
In particular, all weights of $\lambda$ on $V$ are strictly positive.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
. Let
$C=\sum_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}\mathbb R_{\geq0}v_\rho
\subseteq N_{\mathbb R}$,
and let $C^\vee\subseteq M_{\mathbb R}$ be its dual cone.
Inside the group algebra $\overline{K}[M]$, restriction
to the torus identifies
\[
\overline K[X_{\overline K}]
=
\bigcap_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
\overline K[\sigma^\vee\cap M]
=
\overline K[C^\vee\cap M]
\subseteq \overline K[M].
\]
It follows that $C^\vee\cap M=\{0\}$,
and we conclude that $C^{\vee}=0$ since $C^\vee$ is a rational polyhedral cone. Thus $C=(C^\vee)^\vee=N_{\mathbb R}$ by the duality of closed
convex cones.

Consequently,  we have
$-v_\rho\in C$ for every $\rho\in\Sigma(1)$. Choose $b_{\rho\tau}\in\mathbb Q_{\geq0}$ such that
$v_\rho+\sum_{\tau\in\Sigma(1)}b_{\rho\tau}v_\tau=0$.
Summing these relations over $\rho$, we obtain
\[
\sum_{\tau\in\Sigma(1)}
\left(1+\sum_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}b_{\rho\tau}\right)v_\tau=0.
\]
Every coefficient is a strictly positive rational number. Clearing denominators gives positive integers $n_\tau$ such that
$\sum_\tau n_\tau v_\tau=0$.

Let $L/K$ be the splitting field of $T$ and let $\Gamma=\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$. For each $\rho$, let
$a_\rho=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}n_{\gamma^{-1}\rho}$, then we have
\[
\sum_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}a_\rho v_\rho
=
\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}
\sum_{\tau\in\Sigma(1)}n_\tau v_{\gamma\tau}
=
\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}
\gamma\left(\sum_{\tau\in\Sigma(1)}n_\tau v_\tau\right)
=0.
\]

Define $\ell:D\to\mathbb Z$ by $\ell(D_\rho)=a_\rho$, then $\ell$ is
Galois-equivariant. For every $m\in M$, we have
\[
\ell(\delta(m))
=
\sum_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}
a_\rho\langle m,v_\rho\rangle
=
\left\langle m,\sum_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}a_\rho v_\rho\right\rangle
=0.
\]
Hence $\ell$ factors through a Galois-equivariant homomorphism
$\overline\ell:P\to\mathbb Z$.
Taking the dual of $\overline{\ell}$ yields a
$K$-cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbb G_m\to G$.

The composite $\mathbb G_m\xrightarrow{\lambda}G\hookrightarrow R$
is the dual of $\ell:D\to\mathbb Z$.
Consequently, after base change to $\overline K$, the map sends
$t$ to $(t^{a_\rho})_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}$, and its induced action on $V_{\overline{K}}$ is
\[
(z_\rho)_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}
\longmapsto
(t^{a_\rho}z_\rho)_{\rho\in\Sigma(1)}
\]
which proves our claim.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $q:Y\to X$ be the torsor defined in propostion \ref{cox torsor}, and $\lambda:\mathbb{G}_{m}\to G$ be the cocharacter defined in lemma \ref{positive weight}. Then the datum $(G,V,Y,q,\lambda)$
 is a postive linear torsor presentation for $X$. Since $G$ is of multiplicative type, we conclude the result by theorem \ref{main thm}.

label: avoid
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{avoid}
Let $U\subseteq W\simeq\mathbb A_K^n$ be a nonempty open subset such that $\operatorname{codim}_W(W\setminus U)\ge2$. Assume moreover $U$ is stable under
\[
 \lambda(r)(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=(r^{a_1}z_1,\ldots,r^{a_n}z_n),
 \qquad a_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}.
\]
 Let $p:U\to X$ be a $K$-morphism invariant under the action of $\lambda$. Then for any $u,v\in U(K)$, there is a $K$-morphism $f:\mathbb{P}^1_K\to X$ with
\[
 f(p_0)=p(u),\qquad f(p_\infty)=p(v).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Z=W\setminus U$ with its reduced scheme structure, and
let $u=(u_i)$ and $v=(v_i)$ be their coordinates. Let $C=\mathbb A^n_K$ with
coordinates $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ and let $[S:T]$ be the homogeneous coordinates of $\mathbb P^1_K$
with $0=[1:0]$ and $\infty=[0:1]$. Define
\[
F:C\times_K(\mathbb A^2_K\setminus\{0\})\longrightarrow W,
\qquad
F(c,S,T)=
\bigl(u_iS^{2a_i}+c_i(ST)^{a_i}+v_iT^{2a_i}\bigr)_{i=1}^n.
\]
Then $F(c,1,0)=u$, $F(c,0,1)=v$, and $F(c,rS,rT)=\lambda(r^2)F(c,S,T)$.

The ideal of $Z$ is homogeneous for
the grading $\deg z_i=a_i$ since $Z$ is $\lambda$-stable. Thus we may choose weighted homogeneous
generators $h_1,\ldots,h_b$ of weighted degrees
$d_1,\ldots,d_b$. Each $h_j(F(c,S,T))$ is homogeneous of
degree $2d_j$ in $S,T$. Thus these equations define a
closed subscheme
\[
\mathcal M=
\bigl\{(c,[S:T])\in C\times_K\mathbb P^1_K:
F(c,S,T))\in Z\}.
\]
Note that the fibres of $\mathcal{M}\to \mathbb{P}^1$ over $0$ and $\infty$ are empty, since
$u,v\notin Z$.

We identify $D_+(ST)\subseteq\mathbb P^1_K$ with $\mathbb G_m$
via $\tau=T/S$. Consider the morphism
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi:C\times_K\mathbb G_m
&\longrightarrow W\times_K\mathbb G_m,\\
(c,\tau)
&\longmapsto
\left(
\bigl(u_i+c_i\tau^{a_i}+v_i\tau^{2a_i}\bigr)_{i=1}^n,
\tau
\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
It is an isomorphism, with inverse
\[
(z,\tau)\longmapsto
\left(
\bigl(\tau^{-a_i}(z_i-u_i-v_i\tau^{2a_i})\bigr)_{i=1}^n,
\tau
\right).
\]

Under the identification $D_+(ST)\simeq\mathbb G_m$, we have
\[
\mathcal M\cap(C\times_K D_+(ST))
=\Psi^{-1}(Z\times_K\mathbb G_m).
\]
In particular, we have $\dim\mathcal M=\dim Z+1\leq n-1$.

Let $pr_{2}:C\times_K\mathbb P^1_K\to C$
and $B=\operatorname{pr}_2(\mathcal M)$. 
Then $B\neq C$, and we may choose a rational point
$c_0\in(C\setminus B)(K)$.
Then $F(c_0,S,T)\notin Z$ for every geometric point
$(S,T)\neq(0,0)$, thus $F(c_0,-,-)$ factors through $U$.

On the charts $S\neq0$ and $T\neq0$ of $\mathbb{P}_{K}^1$, we write the coordinates
$\tau=T/S$ and $\sigma=S/T$ respectively, and define
\[
\begin{aligned}
f_S:\mathbb A^1_{K,\tau}&\longrightarrow X,
&\tau&\longmapsto p(F(c_0,1,\tau)),\\
f_T:\mathbb A^1_{K,\sigma}&\longrightarrow X,
&\sigma&\longmapsto p(F(c_0,\sigma,1)).
\end{aligned}
\]
On the overlap, we have $\sigma=\tau^{-1}$ and
$F(c_0,\sigma,1)
=\lambda(\sigma^2)F(c_0,1,\sigma^{-1})$.
The $\lambda$-invariance of $p$ gives
$f_T(\sigma)=f_S(\sigma^{-1})$.
Thus these morphisms glue to a $K$-morphism
$f:\mathbb P^1_K\to X$ satisfying
$f(0)=p(u)$ and $f(\infty)=p(v)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The equivalence of (i) and (ii) follows from the fact that:
\[
x\in q^{\xi}(Y^{\xi}(K))\Leftrightarrow [Y_{x}]=\xi\in H^1(K,G).
\]

(ii) implies (iii): This is a direct consequence of (lemma \ref{avoid}).

(iii) implies (iv): Trivial.

(iv) implies (i): If $x,y$ is connected by one chain, let $f:\mathbb P^1_K\to X$ with $f(0)=x$ and $f(\infty)=y$.
Denote $P=Y_x$. The Scheme
\[
  \mathcal T
  :=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}_G
       (P\times_K\mathbb P^1_K,f^*Y)
\]
is a torsor under the smooth $K$-group $\operatorname{Aut}_G(P)$ with
 trivial fibre at $0$.
By \cite[Theorem 7.2.1]{bouthier2025generically}, its fibre at $\infty$ is
also trivial. Thus $Y_y\simeq P=Y_x$, and hence
\[
  \delta_q(x)=\delta_q(y).
\]
In the general case, apply the argument repeatedly. 

Finally, let $\xi\in H^1(K,G)$ be an arbitrary element. By Lemma 3.1,
$V^\xi$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb A_K^{\dim_K V}$.
Since $K$ is infinite, every nonempty
open subset of affine space has a $K$-point. Therefore we may
choose $y\in Y^\xi(K)$ and let $x=q^\xi(y)\in X(K)$. Then
we have $\delta_q(x)=\xi$, thus $\delta_q$ is surjective.
Together with the equivalence of (i) and (iv), we conclude that $X(K)/\sim_{\mathbb{P}^1,\mathrm{ch}} \cong  H^1(K,G)$.
head: environment
